notes: Five independent interactive deliverables bundled into one hard task. reasoning_depth=3: the maze solver must reconstruct an unseen connected grid purely from moved/wall/exit responses, tracking its own position and backtracking to branch points; miscounting a wall probe or a failed batch step silently corrupts the map. dependent_stages=3: the offline --sim routine is debugged against a reference fixture, then the SAME routine must drive the live server on all other instances (one stage depends on the other). interaction_statefulness=3: the adventure must be driven over a real PTY to its ending, the exact ending line captured verbatim, and the game must then be quit via its normal path so the in-memory session flushes to SQLite; killing the process would leave the DB empty. hidden_case_generalization=3: the verifier re-runs /app/solve.py --live on three fresh hidden mazes of different shapes/sizes it never saw. quantitative_correctness=3: the reconstructed map must equal the ground-truth grid char-for-char, ending.txt must equal the exact ending sentence, and the vim layout signature must match exactly. The maximum competency floor across the seven claimed competencies is 'hard' (drive a text adventure to its ending and persist progress), which the overall hard bucket meets.
